title: Constructing and Probing Three-Boundary Booklet Geometries
abstract: Partially entangled thermal states (PETS) provide semiclassical families of black-hole microstates prepared through heavy shell insertions. We extend this shell-state framework and propose three-boundary partially entangled thermal states (PETS$_3$) by replacing the two-index insertion data with a trivalent junction tensor. The corresponding bulk three-boundary booklet geometry is constrained semiclassically by the Israel junction condition, allowing us to identify candidate symmetric and mixed-orientation branches. We verify the self-consistency of this construction by counting states in the symmetric all-black-hole sector. Using a heavy-operator probe, we further estimate the detection-to-universal ratio to be $Z_D/Z_U \simeq 3$, twice the two-boundary value of $3/2$. These results suggest that a fine-tuned probe localized on one boundary can test the proposed three-boundary shell state and potentially distinguish it from its two-boundary counterpart.
summary: This work constructs a theoretical framework for three-boundary black hole microstates ($	ext{PETS}_3$) by generalizing previous two-boundary models. By applying a heavy-operator probe, the authors calculate a diagnostic ratio ($Z_D/Z_U$) that predicts a value of 3 for three boundaries, distinguishing it from the two-boundary case. This suggests a powerful tool for probing the topology of quantum gravitational states.
main_problem: The paper generalizes the description of black hole microstates from two-boundary systems to three-boundary systems, motivated by geometries beyond simple single-manifold duals.
main_result: The three-boundary construction yields a detection-to-universal ratio ($Z_D/Z_U$) of $\simeq 3$, which is exactly twice the value found for the two-boundary case ($3/2$), suggesting a diagnostic tool to distinguish the number of boundaries.
method: The authors use a heavy-operator probe applied to three-boundary Partially Entangled Thermal States ($	ext{PETS}_3$) and constrain the resulting bulk geometry using the Israel junction condition.
model_or_system: The model involves three-boundary booklet geometries, where the state is defined by a trivalent junction tensor and is constrained by multiway Israel junction conditions. The system is analyzed using Euclidean path integrals and state counting techniques.
key_observables: Detection-to-universal ratio ($Z_D/Z_U$), connected overlaps, and the rank of the Gram matrix.
important_parameters: Three-boundary junction tensor, AdS radii ($L_i$), and the effective temperature ($ eta_{	ext{eff}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on an ETH-inspired statistical ansatz for junction amplitudes and approximations based on coarse-graining and saddle-point evaluations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure of 3-shell states and show how the detection-to-universal ratio is calculated using saddle-point contributions from universal and detection geometries.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the $	ext{PETS}_3$ state via a junction tensor, deriving the constraints from the Israel junction condition, and finally calculating the state overlap and the diagnostic ratio $Z_D/Z_U$ using heavy-operator probes.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity/QFT, the methodology of using entanglement structure (PETS) and counting states (Gram matrix rank) to probe geometric properties is highly relevant to understanding entanglement structure in complex quantum systems.
